input.question: How does constant stress affect the body?
input.ground_truth: [Allostatic load](_URL_10_) is essentially the cumulative effect of chronic stress on a human. This effect is believed to exert itself through hormones such as epinephrine. There are multiple papers on the relationship between allostatic load and conditions such as diabetes and heart disease. [Here](_URL_9_) is a paper discussing it in relation to disparities in racial mortality. [Here](_URL_11_) is a paper discussing it in relation to obesity. I have to warn you that I am not very familiar with this topic, and it is a topic which is often brought up in the context of natural or complementary medicine. Validated forms of measuring allostatic load seem to be lacking. So, I would take the above studies with a grain of salt.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How does constant stress affect the body?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a little toy car. When you play with it, sometimes you press the gas pedal a lot, and it goes really fast. That’s like when you feel stressed—a lot of things are happening, and your body gets ready to run or fight, just in case.

But if you keep pressing the gas pedal all the time and never let the car rest, what happens? The car gets really tired, and it might not work as well. Your body is the same way!

When you feel stressed all the time, your body keeps getting ready to run or fight, even when you don’t need to. This can make you feel tired, get headaches, have tummy aches, or even get sick more easily. That’s because your body needs rest to be strong and happy.

So, if your body is stressed all the time, it can get tired and not work as well as it should. That’s why it’s important to take breaks and do things that help you feel calm and relaxed!
